customManagers.description: Go's version, from go.dev's release list: go.mod's `go` directive. The go rule groups it with the Dockerfile's golang images, whose tag and digest the dockerfile manager moves. nix/go.nix overrides nixpkgs' go_1_NN onto it; renovate-pins.yaml derives the source hash.

Node's version, from nodejs.org's release list: engines.node (a `>=` floor) and every setup-node node-version. The node rule groups it with the Dockerfile's node image, whose tag and digest the dockerfile manager moves. nix/node.nix overrides nixpkgs' nodejs_NN onto it; renovate-pins.yaml derives the source hash.

pnpm in the image: the Dockerfile's PNPM_VERSION, installed from npm since Node ships no corepack. The pnpm rule groups it with packageManager and pnpm/action-setup; renovate-pins.yaml checks it agrees with packageManager.

packageRules.description: go.mod's own `go` directive is bumped by the go regex manager, grouped with the golang images; left on, gomod would bump the directive alone in a PR of its own. Same for engines.node and the setup actions' node-version, which the node regex manager owns.
One PR per toolchain: the version from its upstream release list and the Dockerfile's image, tag and digest together. After the docker images group on purpose — the later rule wins.

Docker Hub dates a tag by its last push and official images are rebuilt often, so the 3-day age would hold the image behind the version it follows, splitting the toolchain PR. The release list's own age gate already covers the version.

The PR that moves the locked nixpkgs. It touches no toolchain version: nix/{go,node,pnpm}.nix override nixpkgs' package onto the declared patch while the two differ, and .github/workflows/renovate-pins.yaml drops the override's hashes from nix/toolchains.json once the lock catches up. After the major gate on purpose — the later rule wins, so this overrides the major-update dashboard gate above, which a nixpkgs revision would otherwise sit behind forever.
pnpm: package.json's packageManager field, the setup action in CI and the Dockerfile's PNPM_VERSION. Split, they would be three PRs for one upgrade.

A new Go minor is a new nixpkgs line (go_1_NN), so it waits on the dashboard until nixpkgs packages it; nix/go.nix throws on a line it does not have. Patches open straight away — that is the point of sourcing them from go.dev rather than from the lock.

The pnpm rule above lifts the dashboard gate for the whole group; a pnpm major is a new nixpkgs line (pnpm_NN) and has to wait for it like Go's minor. Node needs no rule of its own: its line is the major, which the generic major gate already holds.
